newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler sees '96 sales up 8 pct to 105 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: Daimler sees '96 sales up 8 pct to 105 bln marks.

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG on Thursday predicted sales would grow at least 8.4 percent this year to more than 105 billion marks, lifting earnings in the second half of the year.

Daimler, Germany's biggest company, said sales in the first nine months of the year grew to 75.9 billion marks from 72.8 billion marks a year earlier, an increase that came largely on the back of its car and truck unit, Mercedes-Benz AG.
Chairman Juergen Schrempp hailed the sales increase as evidence that his plans for streamlining the company and targeting shareholder value where paying off.
"This development confirms the course of focusing on a growth strategy and stronger earnings," Schrempp said in a statement.
Sales at Mercedes-Benz, Daimler's cash cow for years, climbed eight percent to almost 57 billion marks in the first nine months of the year.

Success at Mercedes, which has seen strong demand for its new mid-range car, was tarnished by a dip in sales at Daimler's aircraft unit, Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) which saw sales decline to 8.28 billion marks from 8.91 billion marks a year earlier.
But slashing unprofitable businesses and other streamlining measures helped Daimler return to profit in the first half of this year. It reported an operating profit of 827 million marks.
Daimler is currently considering a massive restructuring aimed at further increasing profitability and said on Wednesday it hoped to finalise such plans at a supervisory board meeting on January 23.

Chief financial officer Manfred Gentz said in a magazine interview on Wednesday it was possible the company could resume paying a dividend this year after not doing so in 1995 for the first time in over four decades.
